notes: Read by one pass per language against the checked-out source (`git grep` for the other uses of a name where a call had to be confirmed). The sample was drawn several times: the first draws found harness bugs, each fixed before the numbers were quoted, and the draw reported here is the one taken from the final harness (it reuses the verdicts of the earlier draws wherever the same pair came up again). Found while sampling and fixed: (1) call wins treated a Go RTA edge for a call through a function value (`t.addEntryFunc(..)` makes RTA list every function stored in the field) as a call of the declaration that stores it, which removed real references and made lidx's matching REFERENCES rows ungradable: 20 of the 31 Go bucket items of the first draw were mis-bucketed (51 pairs of go/syft/tests); only static edges and the compiler's own callee positions count now. (2) TypeScript: the left side of an assignment (`isOldBunVersion = ...`) was counted as a reference (now `assignment_target`); `(Foo as any).prototype[..]` was dropped with the static-access exclusion although it uses the class as a value; a call in a nested arrow and a reference in the enclosing method are one pair after lifting (zod `strict` / `errToObj`). (3) Rust: overloaded operators, derefs and index expressions (`a += b` is `add_assign`) were read as references (now `implicit_call`); a reference in `#[cfg]`-disabled code resolved to a function because rust-analyzer does not see the local declared there (ripgrep `features.push(..)`; now `oracle_refs_cfg_gated`); SCIP columns are UTF-8 byte offsets, so on a line with non-ASCII text a call read as a reference (now `call_on_non_ascii_line`); `Trait::method` resolved by inference to one impl was a wrong pair for lidx's trait-declaration target (now `callee_alts`); references outside any function (`static` tables, closures in a `static`) had no caller and are now keyed at the module; lidx's module-level USES rows with no source line (what it records for `Type::f` in value position) were the whole `caller_not_judged` bucket and are now the named bucket `no_evidence_line` and the miss category `coarse_module_level`. The same byte-column misreading also affects the call oracle (a call after non-ASCII text on the same line is dropped from the call edges); it is left alone here so that the call tables stay as they were, and filed as #476. What remains in the bucket and category verdicts below: every sampled wrong pair is a real lidx error (a getter read, `typeof f`, a call through an `any` cast recorded as a reference, a local variable that shadows a function, a shorthand field bound to a function of the same name), every sampled missed pair is a real reference lidx has no edge for, every sampled correct pair is confirmed in the source, and every bucket exclusion is right. One consequence of call wins worth knowing: a lidx wrong reference that coincides with a real call of the same pair (TypeScript `ReturnType<typeof f>` in a function that also calls `f`) is dropped, not counted wrong.
